title: Wisława Szymborska's birth chart
metaDescription: Wisława Szymborska's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.5° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a trine: the Sun and Jupiter within 0.4°, identity wired to expansion. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 9.5° Cancer: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is the Moon. A water sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Gemini (19.8°), Venus in Gemini (20.6°), Mars in Cancer (21.2°): a mind at home in argument and pattern, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Jupiter hold the closest angle here — a trine, 0.4° wide. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Mercury conjunction Venus at 0.8°, and the Sun conjunction Pluto at 1.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. Mercury in Gemini at 19.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Cancer at 21.2° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Libra at 13.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 5 in water, 3 in air, 1 in fire by element, 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed by modality. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Jupiter and Uranus were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aquarius into Pisces during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.7° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
